market_question: Will Marco Rubio win the 2028 US Presidential Election?
reasoning: At nearly 3 years from the election, Marco Rubio’s true odds of winning the presidency are remote. He lost his only prior national campaign, is not a clear front‑runner for the 2028 Republican nomination (J.D. Vance, Donald Trump Jr., and others appear stronger), and must first secure the nomination and then win a general election. The market’s 13.7% implies a probability usually reserved for a top‑tier candidate in the year of the election, not a long‑shot hopeful.
evidence_points: Rubio’s 2016 presidential bid failed early; he has never demonstrated national primary dominance.
The 2028 Republican field is expected to be deep, including figures like J.D. Vance (Trump’s VP) and other rising populists.
Historical data shows that US senators rarely win the presidency, especially in a cycle as uncertain as 2028.
Intrade/Polymarket odds for individual presidential hopefuls more than two years out are typically in low single digits unless they are the incumbent or deemed inevitable.
sources_consulted: Public statements and current political standing of Sen. Rubio
2028 Republican primary polling and futures markets
